messages:
Ava: Quick question — customer (FinRegCo) wants a temporary per-token rate of $0.0004 for a heavy hosted POC (~20M tokens/day). 2-week trial, low-risk cancel. Is there flexibility to do a hosted per-token override and/or a min monthly charge?

Ravi: Can you share which model & avg/peak seq length? Are they asking a straight per-token cut or a tiered bucket? Any existing commit?

Ava: Model is open-llama-13b-8k (current), avg seq ~1k, peaks ~4k. No commit. They explicitly requested $0.0004/token vs our standard ~ $0.0008 for that model. Also asking about waiving min monthly for the pilot.

Maya: Deal Desk chiming in — one-off per-token cuts below published list require approval. For no-commit pilots we prefer to offer promo credits or a capped discounted tier. Two common patterns: 1) token credits (x tokens free) OR 2) short-term discounted tier with an explicit min monthly floor (e.g., $2k) to limit exposure. We generally don't approve >50% off without GTM manager sign-off.

Chris: Legal / procurement question — will they sign a short SOW/addendum? They said they need answers to their security questionnaire before any pricing talk. That outstanding sec QA is an enterprise blocker.

Ravi: Engineering options to reduce cost exposure: route POC to a quantized variant (q4f) as a cheaper execution path, and set a model-fallback policy once a daily token threshold is hit. We can also enforce request-level rate limits per API key to cap spend.

Ava: I'll forward the security questionnaire they sent this morning. Customer prefers a lower rate vs credits; finance is pushing credits though.

Maya: If the customer insists on a straight per-token override with no commit, require product + revenue ops approval AND an explicit hard cap. Proposal options from Deal Desk: 
- Option A: Promo credits covering expected pilot usage (recommended)
- Option B: Short-term discount to X/token with daily and monthly caps + explicit min floor (e.g., $2k)
We need expected conversion ARR and exec sponsor to justify deeper discounts.

Chris: Also clarify cancellation terms for the trial in the addendum. No auto-renew of pilot discounts.

Ravi: Proposed technical counter-proposal to reduce risk: discount to $0.00055/token (not $0.0004) for 2 weeks, daily hard cap 5M tokens, monthly cap $20k, and require sec QA answers completed before enabling. We can implement fallback to the q4f variant and enforce rate limits via routing policy. Example routing snippet we can push to staging:

```
{
  "policy": "pilot-fallback",
  "primary_model": "open-llama-13b-8k",
  "fallback_model": "open-llama-13b-q4f",
  "daily_token_cap": 5000000,
  "rate_limit_per_min": 20000
}
```

Ava: I'll pitch that to the customer. @Maya can you draft the short addendum? @Ravi can you prepare the routing & rate-limit in staging?

Maya: On it. I'll open a deal desk request and draft a 2-week addendum: https://redwood.internal/deals/new?ref=1814001234 — include expected ARR on conversion, attach the sec questionnaire answers once ready.

dealbot: Deal desk request created: D-7462. Approval required: RevOps + GTM Manager.

Chris: :thumbsup: That keeps exposure reasonable and gives the customer something they can try. If they convert to a commit we can reprice deeper.

Ava: Thanks everyone — follow-ups: Maya -> addendum draft by EOD, Ravi -> staging config and routing policy, I -> send sec QA answers and present counter-proposal to the customer. Will update thread after the call.
